neighbours.label: verbs of wanting and feeling with a personal or generic human subject in reflective or aspirational talk ('what I want', 'you won't feel a sense of …'), as against the same frames about plain facts or actions
fire: If you never stop to rest, you won't feel a sense of calm.
Before choosing a career, ask what you truly want from life.
As a coach I know exactly what I want my players to learn.
Because we care about rivers, we want to keep them clean.
Without real friends, people rarely feel a sense of belonging.
Ask yourself honestly, what do you want your life to look like?
As parents we want our children to grow up kind and curious.
When the work has meaning, you feel a sense of pride every day.
quiet: If you never stop to rest, you won't finish the race on time.
Before choosing a career, ask how many hours the job requires.
As a coach I know exactly when my players arrive at practice.
Because the rivers flood, the town built a new wall last year.
Without real roads, the villages rarely receive fresh supplies.
Ask yourself honestly, what time does the last bus leave?
As parents we drive our children to school every morning.
When the work is finished, you lock the office every day.
